question: What should a nurse typically do after a patient gets a positive result on a screening RDT?

options.A: Start major surgery immediately
options.B: Throw away all the remaining test kits
options.C: Ignore the result and send the patient home
options.D: Perform a confirmatory test if required by guidelines

explanation: Screening tests can sometimes give false positives, so important diagnoses often require a second confirmatory test. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h4)

question: In infection control, what do we call a non-living object like a stethoscope or door handle that can pass germs from one person to another?

options.A: An insect carrying a disease
options.B: A contaminated inanimate object
options.C: The natural home of a pathogen
options.D: A break in the human skin

explanation: Spot on! In nursing, we call these non-living items 'fomites'. They easily pick up germs in the ward and carry them to the next patient if we don't clean our hands or equipment.

question: Which parts of the body are mainly affected by leprosy?

options.A: Bones and joints
options.B: Liver and gut
options.C: Skin and peripheral nerves
options.D: Lungs and upper airways

explanation: The leprosy bacteria love cooler areas of the body, which is why they mainly attack the skin and the nerves outside the brain and spinal cord. You've got this!

question: A patient scheduled for a skin snip is very anxious about pain. What is your best first response?

options.A: Cancel the procedure immediately without consulting the doctor
options.B: Administer general anesthesia to keep the patient completely asleep
options.C: Explain the procedure steps and reassure them about local anesthetic use
options.D: Tell the patient that the procedure is entirely painless and quick

explanation: Great nursing judgement! Walking patients through the steps and letting them know local numbing will be used calms their nerves.

question: What is a very important self-care habit to teach a patient who cannot feel their feet?

options.A: Washing with harsh antiseptic spirit daily
options.B: Checking the feet every single day for cuts and sores
options.C: Walking barefoot to make the soles tougher
options.D: Soaking feet in hot water to boost blood flow

explanation: Since they won't feel pain from a thorn or scrape, daily mirror checks help catch injuries before they turn into bad ulcers. You are learning real patient care!

question: Why do nurses care about picking a good, solid study design?

options.A: It guarantees that funding will be approved by the hospital board
options.B: It allows the researcher to skip the ethical review process entirely
options.C: It ensures the resulting evidence is strong enough to guide safe patient care
options.D: It eliminates the need for any statistical analysis in the project

explanation: Spot on! We want to base our bedside nursing on facts we can truly trust to keep our patients safe and healthy. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why is it important for hospital leadership to show staff that audit data leads to real changes?

options.A: It proves that managers do all the heavy work on the ward
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future ward meetings
options.C: It motivates staff to keep participating honestly in quality data collection
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about their treatment

explanation: When nurses see that their reports actually solve real ward problems, they feel valued and stay excited to help make things better.

question: Why do public health nurses and planners care about measuring disease incidence?

options.A: It provides the exact medical cure for infected patients
options.B: It shows if a disease outbreak is growing or shrinking
options.C: It replaces the need for routine vaccination programs
options.D: It calculates the total hospital building costs needed

explanation: Spot-on! Watching new cases over time helps health teams know if prevention is working or if an epidemic is spreading.

question: Which part of the stethoscope is best suited for hearing low-pitched murmurs like S3 or S4?

options.A: The bell
options.B: The tubing
options.C: The ear pieces
options.D: The diaphragm

explanation: The bell of the stethoscope transmits low-frequency sounds better when held lightly against the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is usually the very first sign that a patient has taken in too much salt?

options.A: Severe yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes
options.B: Sudden and noticeable weight gain from fluid retention
options.C: Immediate development of a high grade fever
options.D: A sudden drop in resting heart rate below 50 beats per minute

explanation: You got it! Because water chases salt, eating too much sodium quickly shows up on the weighing scale as water weight.

question: What is the main sign that a mum is experiencing distress during labour?

options.A: Complete absence of uterine contractions
options.B: A sudden drop in maternal blood pressure
options.C: An increase in fetal heart rate baseline
options.D: Severe physical and emotional exhaustion

explanation: Maternal distress happens when the physical and emotional weight of labour completely overwhelms the mum's coping powers. Spotting this early lets you step in with a comforting touch!

question: Which of these is a very common nutrition challenge during the teenage years?

options.A: Development of eating disorders and poor dietary choices
options.B: Complete lack of appetite caused by hormonal stabilization
options.C: Permanent intolerance to all dairy calcium sources
options.D: Inability to absorb basic proteins from food

explanation: Between body image worries and busy school schedules, teens are extra vulnerable to skipping meals, picking junk food, or struggling with eating habits.

question: In community health, why can't just one type of health worker solve every problem?

options.A: Government policies forbid single-worker clinics
options.B: Doctors lack the training to visit local neighborhoods
options.C: Nurses refuse to handle community cases on their own
options.D: Community issues involve physical, social, and economic factors

explanation: Spot on! Because a patient's health is tied to housing, money, and food, we need a mix of specialists to truly help.

question: Why should you tell a patient that a steroid nasal spray won't clear a stuffy nose instantly like a decongestant spray?

options.A: The body destroys steroid medications before they reach the tissue.
options.B: Steroids work slowly by altering cellular processes over days, not minutes.
options.C: Steroid molecules are too large to absorb through the nasal lining quickly.
options.D: Nasal sprays only work if the patient tilts their head upside down.

explanation: You're right! Steroids change gene expression and protein making inside cells, which takes a few days to show real magic. Patience is key with these sprays!

question: A patient refuses their home exercises and seems down. How should you view this as a nurse?

options.A: They clearly want their condition to deteriorate permanently
options.B: They are purposely wasting the healthcare team's valuable time
options.C: They have no right to question their prescribed care plan
options.D: They are likely overwhelmed and need support rather than judgment

explanation: When patients pull back, it's often burnout or emotional distress speaking. A little empathy goes a long way in helping them trust the process again.

question: Which of these is a macronutrient that our bodies need in large amounts?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Minerals
options.C: Water-soluble enzymes
options.D: Vitamins

explanation: Carbs, proteins, and fats are your macronutrients—the heavy lifters our bodies need in big quantities every day!

question: What is the recommended feeding approach for a healthy infant under six months old?

options.A: Cow milk mixed with cereal in a baby bottle
options.B: Daily introduction of mashed solid family meals
options.C: Pureed vegetables combined with fruit juices
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding or infant formula feeding

explanation: For the first six months of life, breast milk or standard infant formula provides all the necessary nutrients and hydration. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which harmful traditional practice should nurses actively discourage when teaching mothers about diarrhoea?

options.A: Mixing ORS packets in clean drinking water
options.B: Withholding food and fluids to rest the bowel
options.C: Continuing to breastfeed the infant on demand
options.D: Giving zinc supplements for two full weeks

explanation: Never starve a tummy bug! Stopping food and water only makes malnutrition and dehydration worse. Children with diarrhoea need continued feeding and plenty of fluids to heal.

question: When do doctors usually order a polysomnography (sleep study) for a sleep complaint?

options.A: For every patient presenting with simple sleep-onset insomnia
options.B: As a mandatory first step before taking a patient history
options.C: When a secondary sleep disorder like sleep apnea is suspected
options.D: To confirm the diagnosis of acute situational stress

explanation: Standard insomnia doesn't require a sleep study. We order polysomnography when we need to rule out other medical conditions like sleep apnea or restless legs.

question: Why might an elderly patient with osteomyelitis not have a high fever?

options.A: Circulating antibiotics constantly suppress core body temperature
options.B: Their immune response may be blunted, altering classic systemic signs
options.C: Bone infections never cause systemic temperature changes in adults
options.D: Older bones are completely immune to inflammatory pyrogens

explanation: Older adults sometimes have quieter immune systems, meaning they might not show the textbook high fever even when a serious infection is brewing.

question: What part of the male genitalia is removed during circumcision?

options.A: The urethral meatus
options.B: The foreskin
options.C: The penile shaft skin
options.D: The scrotal sac

explanation: Circumcision specifically involves surgically excising the prepuce, or foreskin, that covers the glans penis. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h1)

question: In the TNM cancer staging system, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Malignancy grade
options.B: Microscopic size
options.C: Metastasis
options.D: Mitosis rate

explanation: You've got this! In TNM staging, 'M' tells us if the cancer has traveled or metastasized to other parts of the body.

question: Which surgical treatment provides a permanent cure so fibroids never return?

options.A: Uterine artery embolization
options.B: Hormonal birth control
options.C: Myomectomy
options.D: Hysterectomy

explanation: A hysterectomy removes the entire uterus, meaning fibroids have nowhere left to grow. It's the ultimate definitive cure.

question: Why is placing an unconscious, breathing patient into the recovery position so important?

options.A: It keeps the airway clear and prevents aspiration of fluids
options.B: It stops involuntary muscle spasms in the arms and legs
options.C: It makes it easier to reapply the AED pads if needed
options.D: It lowers the patient's elevated blood pressure quickly

explanation: The recovery position uses gravity to keep the tongue and saliva from blocking the airway of someone who is knocked out. Safety first!

question: Why is depression in older adults so often missed by healthcare providers?

options.A: Its symptoms are often incorrectly blamed on normal aging
options.B: Standard screening tools do not work on people over sixty
options.C: Older adults naturally have higher immunity to sadness
options.D: Depression only affects teenagers and young adults

explanation: It's easy to miss! Signs like fatigue, tiredness, and pulling away from social activities are frequently mistaken for just 'growing old,' leaving depression untreated.

question: Which of the following items should NOT be served on a soft diet?

options.A: Popcorn and potato chips
options.B: Well-cooked white rice
options.C: Mashed Irish potatoes
options.D: Smooth vanilla pudding

explanation: Hard, dry, and crunchy snacks like popcorn and chips can easily scratch the throat or cause choking on a soft diet. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h5)

question: A mother asks why her toddler needs a mix of both animal and plant proteins. What's the best way to answer?

options.A: Mixing them ensures the child gets all the essential building blocks for growth
options.B: Animal proteins contain no essential amino acids on their own
options.C: Plant proteins are toxic to the kidneys of young children
options.D: Only animal proteins can provide energy for daily physical activities

explanation: Spot on. Combining different protein sources helps make sure the child gets every essential amino acid their growing body needs!

question: Why do seasonal rains often cause a drop in immunization coverage in rural areas?

options.A: Dirt roads and broken bridges make travel to health centers difficult
options.B: Rain causes widespread power outages that destroy all vaccine vials
options.C: Mothers are legally forbidden from taking children outside during storms
options.D: Vaccines wash away easily when exposed to heavy rainwater

explanation: Correct! Flooded paths and bad roads physically isolate villages from health centers during the rainy season.

question: Which tissue type burns more calories at rest?

options.A: Bone matrix
options.B: Blood plasma
options.C: Muscle tissue
options.D: Adipose tissue

explanation: Muscle is metabolically active tissue that burns more energy at rest than fat (adipose) tissue. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h5)

question: What does a U&E panel primarily assess in a patient?

options.A: Kidney function and electrolyte balance
options.B: Thyroid hormone production
options.C: Liver enzymes and clotting factors
options.D: Red and white blood cell counts

explanation: A U&E test specifically targets kidney health, hydration levels, and chemical minerals in the blood. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h1)

question: What happens during a uterine perforation?

options.A: An instrument punctures the wall of the uterus.
options.B: The uterine muscle permanently stops contracting.
options.C: Blood clots block the fallopian tubes completely.
options.D: The cervix fails to dilate during surgery.

explanation: Simply put, 'perforation' means a hole. It occurs when a surgical instrument accidentally pokes through the muscular wall of the uterus.

question: Why do nurses track developmental milestones like sitting up and walking in toddlers?

options.A: It determines when the child can stop receiving immunizations
options.B: It proves the child will excel academically in primary school
options.C: Milestones are only used for research and have no clinical value
options.D: Delays can signal underlying neurological, nutritional, or systemic problems

explanation: You got it! Tracking milestones helps you spot delays early so the child can get the right medical help or therapy quickly.

question: What factor most commonly drives teenagers toward dangerous, underground abortion practices?

options.A: Abundant availability of free clinical termination services
options.B: Encouragement from community health committees
options.C: Complete legal protection for all medical procedures
options.D: Strict social stigma, legal restrictions, and lack of safe care access

explanation: Exactly. When judgment, strict laws, and a lack of open support block safe care, desperate teenagers unfortunately turn to risky alternatives.

question: Why is active listening and counseling so important when nursing patients with reproductive issues?

options.A: To make sure they follow hospital visiting hours
options.B: To diagnose mental health disorders on our own
options.C: To replace the need for any surgery or medicine
options.D: To help them talk through emotional pain and body worries

explanation: Wonderful! Reproductive issues can bring deep worry and sadness. Listening to our patients validates their feelings and supports total healing.

question: Why are AROM exercises great for keeping a patient's nervous system working well?

options.A: They require the brain to send nerve impulses that actively contract the muscles.
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for any other physical therapy.
options.C: They stop the patient from ever feeling tired during the hospital stay.
options.D: They force the joints to move past their normal anatomical limits safely.

explanation: Spot on! When the patient initiates the move themselves, the communication highway between the brain and muscles stays open and strong.

question: When must a nurse researcher use non-parametric statistical tests?

options.A: When the research study is funded by a government hospital
options.B: When the data does not follow a normal bell curve distribution
options.C: When the sample size is extremely large and perfectly random
options.D: When all study variables are measured on a continuous scale

explanation: Brilliant! If your data is messy or skewed and doesn't fit that neat bell-shaped curve, non-parametric tests save the day.

question: Which of these is NOT part of a nurse's core responsibility when giving medications?

options.A: Checking the patient for known drug allergies beforehand
options.B: Deciding the wholesale market price for the medication
options.C: Verifying the correct dosage calculation prior to giving it
options.D: Teaching the patient about possible side effects at home

explanation: Pricing medications is up to the pharmacy and hospital administration—your focus is purely on safe, clinical care and patient education!

question: What triggers the cephalic phase of digestion?

options.A: The arrival of food in the small intestine
options.B: The sight, smell, or thought of food
options.C: The stretching of the stomach wall
options.D: The absorption of nutrients in the colon

explanation: The cephalic phase is a reflexive response driven by the brain when we sense food through sight, smell, taste, or even thoughts. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h3)

question: What is usually the very first physical sign of puberty in girls?

options.A: Onset of the first menstrual period
options.B: Rapid widening of the shoulders
options.C: Growth of axillary hair
options.D: Breast bud development

explanation: Correct! The appearance of breast buds is typically the first visible sign that female puberty has kicked off.

question: What does the acronym PAIR stand for in the management of hydatid cysts?

options.A: Preparation, Anesthesia, Isolation, Recovery
options.B: Puncture, Aspiration, Injection, Respiration
options.C: Palpation, Auscultation, Incusion, Repair
options.D: Perfusion, Activation, Irrigation, Removal

explanation: PAIR is a percutaneous technique involving puncturing the cyst, aspirating fluid, injecting a scolicidal agent, and reaspirating. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T25#GNS313_U2_T25_h7)

question: How do distribution bottlenecks contribute to micronutrient deficiencies in remote communities?

options.A: Government clinics ban the distribution of dietary supplements
options.B: Fresh, nutrient-rich foods spoil or become too expensive before arriving
options.C: Farmers deliberately hide vitamins inside processed food items
options.D: Families choose to stop eating locally grown grains completely

explanation: When transport fails, perishable protective foods fail to reach populations, leaving them with monotonous, low-nutrient diets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h7)

question: In what pattern should you clean an injection site with an alcohol swab?

options.A: Up and down in long vertical strokes only
options.B: In a circular motion from the center moving outward
options.C: From the outer edges inward toward the exact center
options.D: In a harsh side-to-side scrubbing motion across the skin

explanation: Cleaning from the center outward pushes dirt and bacteria away from the spot where the needle will enter the skin. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h4)

question: How does the uterus typically feel when assessing a patient with puerperal sepsis?

options.A: Soft, boggy, tender, and larger than expected for the postpartum day
options.B: Displaced entirely to the left side with no tenderness
options.C: Firm, contracted, non-tender, and well below the umbilicus
options.D: Completely rigid like a board with absent bowel sounds

explanation: Infection slows down normal uterine shrinking (involution). Instead of feeling firm, a septic uterus often feels soft, bulky, and painful when you touch it.

question: What is a key safety message nurses should share with families to stop accidental poisonings at home?

options.A: Keep all household cleaning products unlocked on the lower kitchen floor.
options.B: Always induce vomiting immediately if someone smells a strange chemical.
options.C: Mix leftover prescription antibiotics into drinking water to save space.
options.D: Never store dangerous chemicals or fuel in empty food or drink containers.

explanation: This is a classic life-saving tip! Putting fuel or chemicals in juice or soft drink bottles is a major trap for thirsty kids and adults alike.

question: Why do bedside nurses need to know a little bit about hospital finances?

options.A: Every hospital supply and shift hour costs money
options.B: It allows nurses to purchase private equipment for their wards
options.C: Clinical outcomes have no relation to operational budgets
options.D: Nurses are legally required to manage the hospital bank accounts

explanation: Everyday choices on the ward—like how we use supplies or schedule shifts—directly affect the hospital's budget. Great nurses care for both patients and resources!

question: What is the main heart and philosophy behind home health nursing?

options.A: Promoting patient empowerment and self-care within their environment
options.B: Isolating the patient from family members to prevent infection
options.C: Transferring all decision-making power entirely to the physician
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital routines inside private residences

explanation: Well done! It's all about helping patients and their families feel confident to manage their own health right where they live.

question: What is the biggest danger when someone has a severe case of watery diarrhoea?

options.A: Sudden increase in white blood cell count
options.B: Permanent damage to the stomach lining
options.C: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.D: Rapid loss of water and electrolytes

explanation: Frequent watery stools quickly drain the body of vital fluids and salts, which can lead to dangerous dehydration before you know it. Great job keeping watch for this!

question: Which research question is best suited for a quantitative approach?

options.A: What are the emotional challenges of being a first-time ward manager?
options.B: How do patients describe their spiritual journey in palliative care?
options.C: What does it feel like to live with chronic kidney failure?
options.D: Does a 10mg dose of medication lower blood pressure faster than a 5mg dose?

explanation: Because we are measuring dosage amounts and blood pressure numbers, we need a numerical, quantitative study design.

question: Why must nurses in Nigeria ask patients about traditional herbs or local concoctions during a drug history check?

options.A: Local herbs replace the need for checking kidney function tests.
options.B: Traditional mixtures are always completely harmless and speed up healing.
options.C: Herbs can interact with prescription drugs and cause unexpected adverse reactions.
options.D: Hospitals require herbal documentation to qualify for government funding.

explanation: Patients often use local herbs alongside hospital medications. Knowing about them helps us catch and prevent dangerous drug-herb clashes!

question: When is it legally and ethically okay for a nurse to break an adolescent's confidentiality?

options.A: When the adolescent is at risk of severe harm or abuse
options.B: Whenever the patient misses a routine appointment
options.C: When the patient's parents demand to know everything
options.D: Whenever the nurse feels like chatting with colleagues

explanation: That's right! Safety always comes first. If a minor faces extreme danger or abuse, a nurse has a duty to step in and protect them.

question: Why do pregnant women routinely get screened for STIs during early prenatal visits?

options.A: To eliminate common morning sickness symptoms during the first trimester
options.B: To determine the exact biological sex of the unborn infant
options.C: To prevent transmitting infections from the mother to the developing fetus
options.D: To cure congenital genetic abnormalities present at conception

explanation: Exactly! Catching and treating infections early protects the baby from complications during pregnancy and birth.

question: What is the name of the specific space that directly surrounds and protects the human heart?

options.A: cranial cavity
options.B: pleural cavity
options.C: pericardial cavity
options.D: mediastinum cavity

explanation: Think 'peri' for around and 'cardio' for heart! The pericardial cavity is the cozy, fluid-filled space right around your heart.

question: What is the main purpose of a physical examination in nursing?

options.A: To replace the need for a detailed patient medical history
options.B: To diagnose medical conditions independently without a doctor
options.C: To gather objective data about the patient's health status
options.D: To fulfill mandatory hospital paperwork requirements

explanation: A physical examination provides concrete, measurable facts about the body to complement what the patient tells you in their history. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h1)

question: A pregnant woman at a primary health clinic presents with facial swelling, blurred vision, and a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Give her paracetamol tablets and ask her to wait
options.B: Advise her to drink plenty of palm wine and sleep
options.C: Send her home with instructions to rest for a week
options.D: Refer her urgently to a secondary or tertiary facility

explanation: These are signs of severe pre-eclampsia, which can quickly lead to deadly eclamptic seizures if not managed in a hospital. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h4)

question: A community health nurse wants to start a nutrition program in a rural village. What is the best first step following PHC philosophy?

options.A: Build a modern multi-story hospital in the center of the village
options.B: Consult with local community leaders and residents to identify their actual nutritional priorities
options.C: Import expensive foreign dietary supplements and distribute them immediately
options.D: Report the villagers to local authorities for poor feeding habits

explanation: You got it! Community participation always starts by listening to the people first and letting them help identify their own needs and solutions.

question: What is the primary function of a hormone receptor on a target cell?

options.A: To filter hormones out of the bloodstream
options.B: To manufacture and release new hormones
options.C: To break down excess hormones for energy
options.D: To recognize and bind a specific hormone

explanation: Receptors act like specialized locks that only open for their specific hormone key to trigger a cellular response. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h1)

question: What happens to infectious soft waste after it successfully goes through an autoclave cycle?

options.A: It becomes radioactive and needs special deep burial.
options.B: It instantly turns into liquid that pours down the drain.
options.C: It is sterilized and can often be handled like general waste.
options.D: It must still be burned in an open outdoor pit.

explanation: You're doing great! Once an autoclave kills all the infectious germs, the treated waste is safe and no longer poses a biological hazard.

question: A patient says their knee pain gets worse when climbing stairs and feels better when resting. Which part of PQRST is this?

options.A: Pain severity and scale
options.B: Timing and frequency
options.C: Provoking and palliating factors
options.D: Region and radiation

explanation: Well done! Things that trigger pain (like stairs) are provoking factors, and things that soothe it (like rest) are palliating factors.

question: What makes an auto-disable syringe different from a regular disposable syringe?

options.A: It locks automatically after one use to prevent reuse
options.B: It doesn't need a needle to deliver medication
options.C: It can be easily washed and sterilized for another patient
options.D: It is made entirely of recycled plastic

explanation: Exactly right! Auto-disable syringes have a clever built-in stop that keeps the plunger from pulling back a second time, keeping everyone safe.

question: What crucial equipment must be kept right at the bedside after a thyroid surgery?

options.A: An automated external defibrillator machine
options.B: A mechanical ventilation breathing circuit
options.C: A tracheostomy tray and suction equipment
options.D: A continuous positive airway pressure mask

explanation: Correct! Because neck swelling or bleeding can block the airway fast, having emergency airway tools right at hand is an absolute lifesaver.

question: Where is the best place on the chest to listen to the apical pulse with a stethoscope?

options.A: In the center of the sternum right over the xiphoid process
options.B: In the second intercostal space on the right side of the sternum
options.C: Just below the left clavicle near the shoulder joint
options.D: Over the fifth intercostal space at the left midclavicular line

explanation: The tip of the heart points down toward the left. Listening at the fifth space between the ribs, straight down from the middle of the left collarbone, lets you hear it loud and clear!

question: Why are asymptomatic carriers so tricky to deal with during disease outbreaks?

options.A: They develop severe complications that require immediate intensive care unit admission
options.B: They continue normal daily activities and spread the pathogen without knowing they are sick
options.C: They destroy the infection too quickly for laboratory tests to detect any antibodies
options.D: They carry mutated strains of bacteria that are completely immune to all known antibiotics

explanation: Because they don't feel sick, they don't stay home or isolate. They walk around living life normally while unintentionally passing the virus or bacteria along.

question: How can a severe infection in the middle ear or sinuses end up causing a brain abscess?

options.A: By traveling directly through the bloodstream via the auditory nerve sheath
options.B: By causing systemic dehydration that concentrates bacteria in brain tissue
options.C: By eroding through adjacent thin cranial bones into the central nervous system
options.D: By triggering an autoimmune response that attacks the cerebral cortex

explanation: The bone walls separating your sinuses and ears from your brain are surprisingly thin. A severe, unchecked infection can literally wear right through that bone and spread to the brain. Fascinating and crucial to know!

question: What is the most common and versatile suturing technique used for simple emergency lacerations?

options.A: Retention bridge stitch
options.B: Simple interrupted suture
options.C: Subcuticular continuous stitch
options.D: Continuous running lock

explanation: Simple interrupted stitches are quick to place and provide reliable closure where each stitch stands alone. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the most common type of cancer found in the upper respiratory tract?

options.A: Basal cell carcinoma
options.B: Small cell sarcoma
options.C: Adenocarcinoma
options.D: Squamous cell carcinoma

explanation: Most growths in the mouth, throat, larynx, and nose start in the flat squamous cells that line those moist surfaces. Step by step, you are building stellar clinical knowledge!

question: What special type of room ventilation is a must-have for patients on airborne precautions?

options.A: Positive pressure room
options.B: Standard natural ventilation room
options.C: Negative pressure room
options.D: Reverse isolation airflow room

explanation: Spot on! Negative pressure rooms act like a trap—when the door opens, air rushes in instead of letting infectious germs float out into the hospital hallway.

question: Where do water-soluble nutrients go right after they cross the intestinal lining?

options.A: The urinary bladder for excretion
options.B: The gall bladder for storage
options.C: Lacteals in the lymphatic system
options.D: Capillaries leading to the portal vein

explanation: Sugars and amino acids jump straight into the tiny blood capillaries of the villi and head to the liver via the portal vein for processing.

question: Where do nurses mostly interact with patients regarding reproductive health prevention?

options.A: Exclusively in legislative chambers writing health policies
options.B: At the frontline of both community outreach and clinical care settings
options.C: Only within pharmaceutical manufacturing laboratories
options.D: Solely inside international boardrooms managing NGO budgets

explanation: Exactly! Nurses are right there on the frontlines—out in the communities and inside the clinics—making prevention happen every day.

question: Which of these best captures the full picture of injection safety?

options.A: It is limited to washing hands before opening a packaged syringe
options.B: It covers everything from deciding on the route to safe disposal of waste
options.C: It focuses solely on preventing needlestick injuries among medical doctors
options.D: It only refers to the exact moment the needle enters the patient's skin

explanation: Injection safety isn't just one quick action. It's a complete journey—from checking if the injection is needed, to giving it cleanly, to throwing away the sharps properly.

question: A community health nurse is planning outreach for an area with high youth unemployment. What is the main challenge fresh school leavers usually face?

options.A: A lack of practical work experience and job openings
options.B: Excessive mandatory retirement benefits
options.C: Permanent immunity to common community illnesses
options.D: Severe physical decline due to old age

explanation: Spot on! Fresh graduates often struggle in the job market simply because they lack prior experience and vacancies are scarce. You're doing brilliantly! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h3)

question: What is the main goal of the Safe Motherhood Initiative?

options.A: To promote exclusive formula feeding
options.B: To increase the national birth rate
options.C: To reduce maternal mortality and morbidity
options.D: To eliminate the need for traditional birth attendants

explanation: You've got this! The Safe Motherhood framework was set up specifically to lower the rates of death and severe illness linked to pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h1)

question: Why are nurse reports on side effects so crucial even after a drug has been approved for sale?

options.A: Drug manufacturers refuse to test their products before public release
options.B: Clinical trials cannot uncover every rare reaction before a drug is sold
options.C: Pharmacists do not notice any patient reactions inside the dispensary
options.D: Hospitals are legally required to fine patients who experience side effects

explanation: Exactly! Pre-market tests are limited, so frontline nurses are vital for catching rare side effects once real people start taking the medication.

question: Why must a community health nurse look at both the environment and daily lifestyle of a population?

options.A: To trace the exact family tree of every community member
options.B: To understand the wide range of factors influencing public health
options.C: To fulfill government requirements for building new hospitals
options.D: To find out which residents have private health insurance

explanation: Spot on! People's health isn't just about germs; where they live, what they eat, and how they work all combine to shape their overall well-being.

question: How does severe malnutrition negatively impact a community's immune status?

options.A: It directly destroys the skin's physical ability to sweat
options.B: It prevents infants from absorbing breast milk antibodies
options.C: It speeds up the rate at which vaccines expire in storage
options.D: It impairs the body's ability to produce antibodies and immune cells

explanation: Nutrients are the building blocks of the immune system; lacking them stops the body from making enough cells and antibodies. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following tasks is classified as an Activity of Daily Living?

options.A: Banking
options.B: Bathing
options.C: Cooking
options.D: Shopping

explanation: Activities of Daily Living are basic self-care tasks required for personal independence, which include bathing, dressing, eating, and toileting. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h4)

question: When assessing the tummy (abdomen), why must a nurse listen with a stethoscope *before* pressing or feeling around?

options.A: Hospital policy strictly requires listening before touching
options.B: Palpation can alter bowel sounds and mislead the exam
options.C: Auscultation warms up the stethoscope for the patient
options.D: Palpation causes immediate severe pain in all patients

explanation: Think of it this way: if you press on the tummy first, you wake up the intestines and change the sounds! Always listen before you touch.

question: Why should you check for bladder fullness using a scanner or your hands before placing a catheter?

options.A: To numb the urethral canal before inserting the tube
options.B: To confirm there is an actual need to drain urine before invading sterile tissue
options.C: To measure the exact concentration of bacteria inside the bladder
options.D: To determine what size French catheter is required

explanation: Brilliant! Because catheters bring infection risks, we only want to insert one when we are certain the patient's bladder is actually holding urine.

question: What is the main goal of good nutrition in Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Replacing clinical treatments with herbal remedies
options.B: Preventing deficiency diseases and supporting optimal potential
options.C: Eliminating the need for agricultural market regulations
options.D: Reducing the cost of commercial food imports

explanation: You got this! In PHC, good nutrition is all about helping people stay healthy, avoiding illness, and reaching their full body and mind development. Keep it up!

question: How do vision changes in macular degeneration (AMD) differ from cataracts?

options.A: AMD affects side vision first, while cataracts ruin night vision.
options.B: AMD causes sudden total blindness overnight, while cataracts take years.
options.C: AMD affects central vision, while cataracts cause overall blurriness and glare.
options.D: AMD causes intense eye pain, whereas cataracts are painless.

explanation: Macular degeneration targets your sharp central focus (like when reading), leaving side vision alone. Cataracts, on the other hand, just make everything look foggy and hazy.

question: As a nurse, what should you NEVER do while a patient is actively having a fit?

options.A: Time how long the seizure lasts
options.B: Force objects between the patient's teeth
options.C: Loosen tight clothing around the neck
options.D: Clear hard objects away from the body

explanation: Never put anything in their mouth! You might accidentally chip their teeth, cut their gums, or block their airway even more. Just keep them safe and let the seizure run its course.

question: Which simple tool does a community health nurse use to listen to the baby's heartbeat during a home visit?

options.A: A sphygmomanometer
options.B: An ophthalmoscope
options.C: A percussion hammer
options.D: A Pinard stethoscope

explanation: A Pinard stethoscope (or portable Doppler) is your trusty companion in the field for checking fetal heart tones!

question: You spot an infusion pump cord stretched tightly across a busy hospital walkway. What should you do right away?

options.A: Cover the cord with a wet towel to make it more visible
options.B: Leave it alone because pumps need power to stay functional
options.C: Unplug the pump and run it entirely on low battery power
options.D: Reroute the cord safely out of the walkway to prevent tripping

explanation: Cords across walkways are dangerous tripping hazards for staff and visitors. Moving it safely out of the way keeps everyone walking safely!

question: Which of these is a major threat that can crash a Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Issuing drugs on informal credit to friends and colleagues
options.B: Keeping the pharmacy windows open for ventilation
options.C: Writing clear dosage instructions on drug packs
options.D: Conducting weekly physical counts of medicine boxes

explanation: Giving drugs out on 'friendship credit' drains the cash drawer fast, making it impossible to restock. Business and friendly favors don't mix here!

question: Which germ causes leprosy?

options.A: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.B: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.C: Mycobacterium leprae
options.D: Treponema pallidum

explanation: Spot on! Leprosy is caused by Mycobacterium leprae. It loves to hang out in cooler parts of the body like the skin and outer nerves.

question: A patient falls ill with typhoid after drinking contaminated water. What type of transmission is this?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Indirect transmission
options.C: Airborne transmission
options.D: Direct transmission

explanation: You got it! Because the water acted as a vehicle between the source and the patient, it counts as indirect transmission.

question: A public health nurse hands out mosquito nets to prevent malaria. Which part of the epidemiological triad is this mainly targeting?

options.A: Incubation period
options.B: Agent
options.C: Host genetics
options.D: Environment

explanation: Spot on! Mosquito nets create a physical block between you and the environmental vector, modifying the surrounding environment where disease transmission happens.

question: Who primarily handled the care of sick family members in most ancient households?

options.A: Professional monastic orders
options.B: Government-certified physicians
options.C: Women within the home
options.D: Trained military nurses

explanation: Before formal institutions, caring for the sick was mainly a domestic duty performed by female family members. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to monitor blood levels for drugs with a narrow therapeutic index?

options.A: To calculate the drug's half-life
options.B: To measure liver enzyme production
options.C: To check if the patient is taking food
options.D: To prevent accidental toxicity

explanation: Because the safe zone is so narrow, checking blood levels helps us catch any dangerous buildup before it harms our patient.

question: A client with active breast cancer asks for an injectable contraceptive. How is this classified under WHO guidelines?

options.A: Category 4
options.B: Category 3
options.C: Category 1
options.D: Category 2

explanation: Because breast cancer is sensitive to hormones, using hormonal contraceptives is unsafe and falls into the restricted Category 4.

question: What is the main goal of public health laws for food businesses?

options.A: To collect high taxes from commercial food business owners
options.B: To limit the number of small restaurants operating in local communities
options.C: To standardize recipe ingredients across different cultural restaurants
options.D: To establish minimum safety and sanitation rules that protect the public

explanation: Public health rules set clear hygiene and facility standards to prevent widespread food poisoning. You've got this down!

question: Which surveillance type relies on healthcare workers sending routine reports without special prompting?

options.A: Active surveillance
options.B: Sentinel surveillance
options.C: Passive surveillance
options.D: Syndromic surveillance

explanation: Passive surveillance relies on routine reporting by clinics and hospitals without outside prompting, making it simple but prone to underreporting. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h2)

question: Why should you avoid giving ergometrine to a mother with severe high blood pressure?

options.A: It triggers immediate and uncontrollable uterine relaxation
options.B: It completely stops all breast milk production permanently
options.C: It causes a dangerous spike in maternal blood pressure
options.D: It neutralizes the effects of routine postpartum antibiotics

explanation: Exactly! Ergometrine narrows blood vessels, which can dangerously shoot up blood pressure and put a hypertensive mother at risk of stroke.

question: What is found on an intervention flow sheet?

options.A: The personal financial history and bank details of the client
options.B: The architectural blueprint of the client's residential building
options.C: A detailed biography of the client's childhood and schooling
options.D: A chronological log of treatments, medications, and nursing procedures

explanation: Flow sheets are designed for quick recording of routine, repetitive care tasks like vital signs and medication administration over time. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h3)

question: What happens when organic matter like blood is left on a surface during disinfection?

options.A: It turns the disinfectant into a complete sterilizing agent
options.B: It neutralizes the chemical and shields microbes from contact
options.C: It helps the disinfectant spread more evenly over tools
options.D: It speeds up the chemical reaction time on the surface

explanation: Blood and body fluids are tricky—they absorb the disinfectant and act like a little bunker, protecting the bacteria hiding underneath. Always wash first!

question: How does the sympathetic nervous system react during active labour?

options.A: It stops breathing movements to rest the diaphragm
options.B: It lowers body temperature to conserve cellular fuel
options.C: It shuts down all sensory perception to force sleep
options.D: It increases heart rate, blood pressure, and energy output

explanation: Think of the 'fight-or-flight' response! It kicks in during labour to give the body the extra energy and push it needs for delivery.

question: Where does fertilization of an egg by a sperm normally happen?

options.A: Uterine cavity
options.B: Surface of the ovary
options.C: Fallopian tube
options.D: Vaginal canal

explanation: Correct! The sperm and egg usually meet and fuse right there in the fallopian tube on their journey.

question: Why is the powerful drug Amphotericin B kept strictly for severe, life-threatening fungal infections?

options.A: It is completely ineffective against superficial mucosal yeast infections
options.B: It must be mixed with specific dietary fats to work properly in the body
options.C: It causes severe allergic reactions in every patient who takes it
options.D: It carries a significant risk of serious organ toxicity, especially to the kidneys

explanation: Amphotericin B is famously strong ("Ampho-terrible" to the kidneys!), so doctors only use it when things are really serious.

question: Why is writing down complete notes about pain care so important for nurses?

options.A: It replaces the need to talk directly with the patient.
options.B: It is only required for legal protection during lawsuits.
options.C: It ensures safe continuity of care and evaluates if treatment worked.
options.D: It allows the hospital to bill insurance companies faster.

explanation: Clear notes help the whole healthcare team see what worked, keep the patient safe, and coordinate the next steps smoothly.

question: What usually happens to the endocrine functions of the kidneys when renal tissue becomes damaged?

options.A: Hormone production stops completely within a few hours
options.B: Hormone production increases to compensate for damage
options.C: Hormone production decreases alongside filtering capacity
options.D: Hormone production remains completely normal forever

explanation: When kidney tissue is injured, both its filtering ability and its hormone-producing capabilities decline together. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h1)

question: How has the primary role of the nurse changed from early historical times to today?

options.A: It evolved from informal domestic charity to an autonomous regulated profession
options.B: It changed from independent medical diagnosis to unpaid domestic work
options.C: It shifted from hospital administration to strictly religious duties
options.D: It transformed from a male-only military role to a purely clerical office job

explanation: Think about how far we've come! Modern nursing requires formal education, licensing, and independent critical thinking, rather than just basic home caregiving. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why do doctors often order a Complete Blood Count (CBC) when investigating stubborn fatigue?

options.A: To measure the exact resting metabolic rate
options.B: To quantify circulating central nervous system neurotransmitters
options.C: To detect abnormal levels of thyroid hormones
options.D: To check for anemia and rule out infection

explanation: Spot on! A CBC helps us check red blood cells for anemia and white blood cells for hidden infections, giving us clues about why the patient feels so drained.

question: What is a key benefit of offering structured social activities in assisted living?

options.A: Replacing the need for family visits altogether
options.B: Reducing the cost of building maintenance
options.C: Combating feelings of loneliness and depression
options.D: Eliminating the need for any routine medical care

explanation: Group activities and social events help keep residents engaged, active, and emotionally connected, reducing isolation and depression. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h6)

question: A stroke patient is having trouble swallowing food safely and speaks with slurred words. Who should you call first?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Medical social worker
options.C: Orthopedic surgeon
options.D: Dietitian

explanation: You got it! Speech-language pathologists are the experts when it comes to sorting out both communication troubles and swallowing (dysphagia) issues.

question: A 55-year-old patient complains of constant tiredness, low mood, and fewer morning erections over the past year. What should you suspect?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Acute prostatitis
options.C: Andropause
options.D: Testicular torsion

explanation: When a middle-aged man reports ongoing fatigue, low spirits, and sexual changes, it's a classic pointer toward andropause hormone shifts.

question: You want villagers to remember proper handwashing steps after an outreach. What is the most practical action to take?

options.A: Distribute illustrated posters showing handwashing steps to take home or place in public areas
options.B: Write the medical names of bacteria on a chalkboard during a one-hour lecture
options.C: Tell the villagers to memorize the steps by repeating them three times in silence
options.D: Ask the village head to verbally test every single resident on handwashing theory

explanation: Pictures speak volumes! Visual posters give people a daily reminder so healthy hygiene habits actually stick.

question: Who are typical members of an interdisciplinary community health team?

options.A: Environmental health officers, social workers, and nurses
options.B: Surgeons, pharmacists, and medical equipment vendors
options.C: Private legal practitioners and financial auditors
options.D: Only registered nurses and hospital administrators

explanation: You got it! Community health brings together different experts like nurses, social workers, and environmental officers to tackle all angles of wellness.

question: What is the main danger when a patient stops taking her antibiotics halfway just because she feels better?

options.A: Surviving germs can multiply and cause drug resistance
options.B: The laboratory will lose the record of her initial test
options.C: The patient will instantly develop a severe viral illness
options.D: Her body will stop producing any natural red blood cells

explanation: Stopping early kills off the weak germs but leaves the strongest ones alive to bounce back stronger and harder to treat!

question: Why are the veins in the lower part of the oesophagus so critical during liver disease?

options.A: They prevent stomach acid from washing backward into the throat.
options.B: They supply the main nerve impulses that trigger swallowing waves.
options.C: They carry all arterial blood returning from the entire stomach.
options.D: They form a direct connection between portal and systemic veins.

explanation: Well done! Because these veins link the liver's portal system to the general body circulation, they can bulge and bleed dangerously when liver scarring blocks blood flow.

question: Which mental health challenge is very common among young brides who are cut off from their friends?

options.A: Bipolar manic episodes
options.B: Schizophrenic hallucinations
options.C: Depression and anxiety
options.D: Obsessive compulsive rituals

explanation: Loneliness, losing their childhood, and heavy adult responsibilities often trigger deep depression and anxiety in young wives.

question: Which common class of medications is well known for pushing a patient's blood sugar up?

options.A: Corticosteroids
options.B: Diuretics
options.C: Antibiotics
options.D: Antacids

explanation: Drugs like prednisolone make the body less sensitive to insulin and push the liver to make more sugar. Good to watch out for in clinical practice!

question: Which Nigerian body is in charge of registering nurses and looking after our professional discipline?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration

explanation: Spot on! The NMCN is our very own guardian angel body set up by law to guide nursing training and practice right here in Nigeria.

question: What is the primary role of the cerebellum in the nervous system?

options.A: Coordinating smooth muscle movement and balance
options.B: Processing conscious thoughts and logical reasoning
options.C: Regulating basic body temperature and hunger
options.D: Relaying pain signals from the skin to the brain

explanation: The cerebellum ensures that physical movements are smooth, balanced, and properly timed. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why should nurses check on the emotional well-being of brothers and sisters in a family affected by cerebral palsy?

options.A: Parents usually ignore the affected child to focus entirely on healthy siblings
options.B: Siblings must legally take over financial caregiving once they turn eighteen
options.C: Siblings are at high risk of developing cerebral palsy themselves
options.D: Siblings can experience feelings of neglect, stress, or added responsibilities

explanation: A chronic condition affects the whole household. Siblings often need emotional support to handle changing roles and big feelings.

question: Why did governments start using public insurance to fund home health care programs?

options.A: To discourage families from taking care of relatives at home
options.B: To reduce the high financial burden of long-term hospital stays
options.C: To completely replace traditional doctors with visiting nurses
options.D: To stop the construction of new community health clinics

explanation: Governments figured out that home care is usually much cheaper than keeping patients in acute care hospital wards for weeks of recovery.

question: Why is the involvement of traditional and religious leaders crucial when planning community health interventions?

options.A: They are legally required to sign every nurse's monthly salary voucher
options.B: They provide international grants for buying hospital equipment
options.C: They help build trust and dismantle cultural resistance among community members
options.D: They possess formal training in advanced surgical procedures

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold massive influence over local beliefs and behavior, making them key allies in overcoming health rumors. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)

question: Which of these is a main reason a doctor would order a barium enema?

options.A: Elevated liver enzymes and yellow skin jaundice
options.B: Unexplained chronic diarrhea and rectal bleeding
options.C: Severe dehydration from upper GI bleeding
options.D: Sharp lower right belly pain caused by appendicitis

explanation: Doctors use barium enemas to investigate ongoing lower bowel problems like bleeding or long-term changes in stool patterns.

question: Why are predictive equations used in hospital wards instead of direct calorimetry?

options.A: Calorimetry machines do not measure oxygen
options.B: Formulas are practical and easy to calculate using basic measurements
options.C: Calorimetry chambers are required by law
options.D: Equations are always 100% error-free for everyone

explanation: Using formulas gives nurses a fast, helpful estimate without needing complex or expensive test equipment right at the bedside.

question: Why is the first few weeks after birth a critical time to watch new mothers closely?

options.A: Severe complications like heavy bleeding and infections happen most often then
options.B: Hormone levels drop to zero immediately after birth
options.C: Babies cry constantly during the first few days
options.D: Mothers are usually discharged before labor pain stops completely

explanation: You've got this! Life-threatening emergencies such as heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) and infections are most common right after delivery, which is why close nursing monitoring is so essential. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h1)

question: How would a patient most likely contract iatrogenic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease?

options.A: Through a contaminated surgical tool
options.B: Through a mosquito bite in a tropical zone
options.C: By inheriting a mutated genetic trait
options.D: By eating undercooked beef products

explanation: You nailed it! 'Iatrogenic' means it happened accidentally during a medical or surgical procedure, such as using instruments that previously touched infected tissue.

question: Which part of the heart acts as its main natural pacemaker?

options.A: Purkinje fibers
options.B: Atrioventricular node
options.C: Sinoatrial node
options.D: Bundle of His

explanation: Think of the Sinoatrial (SA) node as the heart's natural spark plug! It fires the electrical impulses that set the rhythm for the whole heart.

question: An older adult is crying and terrified about surgery tomorrow. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Allowing a family member to stay close and offering a calm presence
options.B: Leaving the patient alone so they can sort out their thoughts
options.C: Insisting that the patient goes to sleep immediately without talking
options.D: Telling them that surgery is completely risk-free

explanation: Spot on! Having a loved one nearby and knowing a caring nurse is right there brings huge emotional comfort.

question: Why do hospitals immediately isolate patients showing respiratory symptoms?

options.A: To speed up the administration of intravenous fluids
options.B: To reduce the cost of diagnostic testing supplies
options.C: To prevent transmission to staff and other patients
options.D: To allow patients to sleep without hospital noise

explanation: Isolating patients right away stops airborne droplets from spreading to other vulnerable people in the clinic. Smart nursing practice! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h4)

question: A patient with terminal cancer talks about missing her daughter's wedding next year. What type of grief is this?

options.A: Exaggerated grief
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Collective grief
options.D: Disenfranchised grief

explanation: Spot on! Mourning future events or losses before they actually take place is a clear sign of anticipatory grief. Great clinical thinking!

question: Which Nigerian agency is heavily involved in regulating drug safety and distribution?

options.A: Nigerian Meteorological Agency
options.B: National Youth Service Corps
options.C: NAFDAC
options.D: Federal Road Safety Corps

explanation: NAFDAC is the primary federal agency responsible for regulating and controlling the manufacture, importation, and sale of drugs in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the primary hormone secreted by the hypothalamus that starts the reproductive hormone chain?

options.A: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.D: Testosterone

explanation: The hypothalamus releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the pituitary gland, which drives the entire reproductive hormone pathway. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h1)

question: What is a great way to help an elderly patient remember their daily meds?

options.A: Using a labeled weekly pill organizer and daily routine cues
options.B: Hiding the pills in food without telling the patient
options.C: Instructing them to double the dose whenever they feel worse
options.D: Telling them to stop taking all drugs if they feel normal

explanation: Pill boxes and tying meds to meal times make life so much easier for patients managing multiple prescriptions.

question: Which patient factor would usually make someone a poor candidate for deep brain stimulation surgery?

options.A: Significant cognitive impairment or dementia
options.B: Intolerable side effects from oral levodopa therapy
options.C: Severe motor fluctuations and on-off periods
options.D: Persistent resting tremor despite high medication doses

explanation: Surgery like DBS requires a clear mind to handle the device and follow-up care. If a patient already has severe memory or thinking issues (dementia), the surgery can sometimes make those worse.

question: What surgical instrument is typically used during a standard laparoscopy for tubal ligation?

options.A: A lighted camera scope and small grasping tools
options.B: A large open abdominal retractor and surgical saw
options.C: A long uterine curette inserted through the vagina
options.D: An ultrasound probe placed directly on the ovaries

explanation: Laparoscopy relies on a small camera inserted via a tiny umbilical incision to guide specialized instruments that seal or block the tubes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h4)

question: In Nigeria, which animal is the main reservoir for the Lassa fever virus?

options.A: Stray domestic dogs
options.B: The multimammate rat
options.C: Domestic dairy cattle
options.D: Migratory waterfowl

explanation: Correct! The multimammate rat is the primary natural reservoir for Lassa fever, shedding the virus in its urine and droppings.

question: What does the golden nursing rule 'if it wasn't documented, it wasn't done' mean in a court of law?

options.A: Unwritten care cannot be proven to have been given in a court of law
options.B: Verbal reports to doctors hold more legal weight than written notes
options.C: Documentation is more important than actually speaking to the client
options.D: Nurses do not need to perform procedures if they write about them

explanation: Legally, courts rely on written records. If an action is missing from the client's file, it is legally considered not to have happened!

question: What effect does severe maternal hypertension or pre-eclampsia typically have on foeto-placental exchange?

options.A: It makes the placental membrane thicker to block toxins
options.B: It increases surface area and speeds up nutrient transfer
options.C: It reduces blood flow and decreases exchange efficiency
options.D: It has no noticeable impact on fetal circulation

explanation: Hypertension causes vessel constriction in the mother's uterus, lowering blood flow to the placenta and starving the fetus of optimal oxygen and nutrients. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h8)

question: What is the main idea behind the 'One Health' approach to disease control?

options.A: Focusing solely on human hospital care during a disease outbreak
options.B: Treating every infectious disease with a single universal antibiotic
options.C: Eliminating all wild animals to protect human settlements entirely
options.D: The interconnected health of humans, animals, and the environment

explanation: One Health reminds us that human health is tied to the health of our animals and our shared environment. We have to look at the big picture!

question: What is the gold-standard test to confirm a patient truly has gout?

options.A: Performing a standard chest X-ray on the patient
options.B: Measuring the daily protein intake in the diet
options.C: Checking a routine blood pressure reading in the clinic
options.D: Examining joint fluid under a microscope for crystals

explanation: You got it! Drawing a little fluid out of the angry joint and spotting those sneaky uric acid crystals under a microscope gives a 100% definite diagnosis.

question: A nurse wants to travel abroad for an 18-month post-basic nursing degree while keeping their job. What should they apply for?

options.A: Mandatory maternity leave status
options.B: Standard annual vacation leave
options.C: Compassionate emergency absence
options.D: Study leave with or without pay

explanation: For long-term academic programs, you must officially apply and get approval for study leave through administrative channels.

question: Why is a psychosocial assessment vital for clients with neurologic conditions?

options.A: Nerve damage and brain injury affect thinking, mood, and daily life.
options.B: It is the only legal way to discharge a patient from the hospital.
options.C: Physical therapy cannot start until mental health is fully cured.
options.D: It replaces the need for a standard physical doctor's examination.

explanation: Brain and nerve disorders directly alter a person's behavior, emotions, and interactions, making psychosocial evaluation just as important as physical care. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is the main goal of preventive reproductive health services?

options.A: To treat infertility using modern assisted reproductive technology
options.B: To cure advanced stages of reproductive tract cancers
options.C: To stop health problems before they start through screening and education
options.D: To manage high-risk surgical emergencies in labor wards

explanation: Preventive services aim to intercept diseases early or stop them entirely using vaccines, screenings, and education. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which body structure is hurt when someone suffers a sprain?

options.A: Tendon
options.B: Muscle
options.C: Cartilage
options.D: Ligament

explanation: A sprain happens when a ligament gets stretched too far or tears. Remember: ligaments connect bone to bone at your joints! You've got this.

question: Which cells in the pancreas make insulin?

options.A: Beta cells
options.B: Acinar cells
options.C: Delta cells
options.D: Alpha cells

explanation: Spot on! Beta cells in the pancreas are the ones responsible for producing insulin to bring your blood sugar down.

question: What does the Swiss Cheese Model of safety explain?

options.A: How hospital kitchens prevent foodborne bacterial illnesses
options.B: The best dietary guidelines for recovering hospital patients
options.C: The step-by-step process of cleaning surgical instruments
options.D: How multiple system failures align to cause an accident

explanation: Think of safety layers like slices of Swiss cheese. Accidents only happen when the holes in every single slice line up at the same time!

question: How does your blood protect your body against germs and infections?

options.A: By increasing the total volume of red blood cells
options.B: By filtering toxins directly through the skin
options.C: By lowering blood pressure during an illness
options.D: By circulating white blood cells and antibodies

explanation: Exactly! Your bloodstream acts like a highway, rushing white blood cells and antibodies straight to wherever germs are trying to attack.

question: What term describes the wear and tear on the body from long-term, ongoing stress?

options.A: Systemic exhaustion
options.B: Adverse adaptation
options.C: Allostatic load
options.D: Homeostatic balance

explanation: 'Allostatic load' is just a fancy way of saying your body gets tired and worn down from fighting stress day after day without a break.

question: Your patient wants to run an extension cord under their bedroom rug to plug in a lamp. What should you tell them?

options.A: Cover the cord with heavy plastic tape for extra safety
options.B: Do not run cords under rugs because heat can build up and cause a fire
options.C: Ensure the carpet is made of synthetic material before placing the cord
options.D: Use a longer extension cord to reach around the carpet edge

explanation: Rugs trap the heat inside electrical cords, which can melt the wires and start a hidden fire. Always keep cords out in the open!

question: What is a common source of emotional stress for school-aged children?

options.A: Academic pressure and peer bullying
options.B: Excessive amounts of physical exercise
options.C: Access to clean drinking water
options.D: Frequent participation in school sports

explanation: Spot on! Hard schoolwork and issues with classmates are major stressors that can weigh heavily on a child's mental health.

question: Why is it so important to rinse the hair thoroughly after shampooing?

options.A: Leftover soap residue can cause scalp irritation and dryness
options.B: Unrinsed shampoo actively accelerates hair follicle growth
options.C: Remaining soap prevents the hair from absorbing water
options.D: Residue permanently changes the natural color of the hair

explanation: Leaving soap behind can dry out the skin and make the scalp itchy and flaky. A good rinse keeps your patient comfortable! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h3)

question: A woman has just delivered her baby ten minutes ago, and you are waiting for the placenta to separate. Which stage of labor is she currently in?

options.A: Third stage
options.B: Fourth stage
options.C: First stage
options.D: Second stage

explanation: The third stage of labor begins immediately after the baby is born and lasts until the complete delivery of the placenta. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h3)

question: Who opened the first birth control clinic in the United States in 1916?

options.A: Florence Nightingale
options.B: Clara Barton
options.C: Mary Seacole
options.D: Margaret Sanger

explanation: Margaret Sanger was a key pioneer who fought legal battles to open the first birth control clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h3)

question: Which body change happens as people grow older that tends to slow down drug clearance?

options.A: Faster production of stomach acid
options.B: Increased total body water volume
options.C: Enlarged total liver mass capacity
options.D: Decreased kidney filtration function

explanation: As we age, kidney function naturally slows down a bit. This means older adults take longer to clear medications from their system. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which nursing action is most important for tracking fluid buildup in a patient with heart inflammation?

options.A: Doing reflex checks on both arms
options.B: Checking the patient's vision every four hours
options.C: Testing grip strength twice a day
options.D: Checking daily weights and tracking intake and output

explanation: Tracking daily weights and fluid charts is your best early warning system for fluid retention and failing heart function. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h6)

question: A cancer patient says food smells too strong and tastes like metal. What is a helpful nursing tip?

options.A: Suggest serving foods cool or at room temperature to reduce strong smells
options.B: Tell the patient to force themselves to eat large portions anyway
options.C: Advise the patient to stop eating completely until treatment ends
options.D: Recommend adding extra iron supplements to every meal

explanation: Warm foods release strong vapors that trigger nausea. Serving meals cool helps hide those metallic tastes and smells. Clever nursing care!

question: What is the proper way to position an adult's ear before putting in ear drops?

options.A: Pull the pinna up and back before instilling the drops
options.B: Keep the client sitting upright for thirty minutes after
options.C: Insert the dropper tip firmly deep into the ear canal
options.D: Pull the earlobe straight down before putting in drops

explanation: Correct! Pulling the pinna up and back opens up the canal so the drops slide right down nicely toward the eardrum.

question: Why can blocking dopamine in the tuberoinfundibular pathway lead to higher prolactin levels?

options.A: Prolactin is converted into dopamine in the bloodstream
options.B: Dopamine directly stimulates the pituitary gland to produce milk
options.C: Blockade destroys the cells that store prolactin
options.D: Dopamine normally acts to inhibit prolactin release

explanation: Normally, dopamine acts like a brake on prolactin. When antipsychotics block that dopamine, you take the brake off, and prolactin levels rise.

question: Why should you avoid using cold compresses to treat pain during a sickle cell crisis?

options.A: Refrigerated items increase the risk of skin breakdown over swollen joints
options.B: Cold temperatures cause blood vessels to constrict and promote further sickling
options.C: Low temperatures stop intravenous pain medications from working properly
options.D: Cold packs numb the skin so the patient cannot feel if the pain is improving

explanation: Remember: cold makes blood vessels narrow (vasoconstriction). This slows down blood flow even more, making the sickled cells clump together worse and increasing the patient's pain.

question: Through which part of the spinal cord do outgoing motor signals leave?

options.A: Dorsal root
options.B: Dorsal root ganglion
options.C: Central canal
options.D: Ventral root

explanation: While sensory signals enter through the dorsal side, motor instructions head out to the muscles through the ventral root at the front.

question: Why are regular walkthrough inspections so important for an occupational health nurse?

options.A: To discipline workers who fail to wear proper uniforms
options.B: To check the financial profits of the plant
options.C: To replace safety officers during their annual leave
options.D: To observe daily work tasks and identify unaddressed environmental risks

explanation: Exactly! Walking through the workspace lets you spot hidden dangers that workers might just get used to and forget to report.

question: A patient wanting a medical abortion has an IUD in place. What should the nurse make sure happens first?

options.A: Ensure the IUD is removed prior to starting the misoprostol regimen
options.B: Leave the IUD in because misoprostol will push it out
options.C: Give extra antibiotics to stop local infections
options.D: Switch the patient immediately to vacuum aspiration

explanation: We need to take out any IUD before starting treatment to prevent serious infections or heavy bleeding. Simple and important safety step!

question: Which of these is NOT a sign of a dangerous, severe allergic reaction to contrast dye?

options.A: Widespread itchy hives on the skin
options.B: Mild metallic taste in the mouth
options.C: Sudden difficulty in breathing
options.D: Swelling of the lips and tongue

explanation: A metallic taste is totally normal! Hives, swollen lips, and trouble breathing, however, are red flags that mean we need to act fast.

question: Why is taking HIV medications right on schedule every single day so crucial?

options.A: Inconsistent timing causes permanent damage to the patient's liver enzymes
options.B: It ensures the pharmacy dispenses the correct refill amount each month
options.C: Missing doses lets drug levels drop, allowing the virus to mutate and resist the medication
options.D: Taking pills late instantly destroys all white blood cells in the body

explanation: Exactly! If drug levels in the blood drop too low, the virus wakes up, multiplies, and figures out how to fight off the drugs.

question: A patient arrives at the ward with a large amount of cash and expensive jewelry. What should the nurse do first regarding these valuables?

options.A: Tell the patient to wear the jewelry so nobody can steal it
options.B: Lock the cash inside the bedside table drawer and keep the key
options.C: Place the items in the open utility room for safe keeping
options.D: Follow hospital policy to document and secure the items safely

explanation: Valuables must be documented on an inventory list and stored securely according to hospital protocol, preferably sent home with family or locked in the main safe. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: What must happen before a public sector nurse moves from probation to a permanent staff member?

options.A: Direct purchase of a permanent tenure certificate from the ministry
options.B: Automatic time elapsed without any evaluation of clinical skills required
options.C: Satisfactory completion of the probation period and positive supervisor evaluations
options.D: Completion of mandatory political party membership registration

explanation: To get confirmed permanently, you need to spend the required time on the job and get good reviews from your supervisors.

question: A patient needs a very early pregnancy test using urine. Which sample should you tell her to collect?

options.A: First morning urine
options.B: Timed two-hour urine
options.C: Random afternoon urine
options.D: Post-exercise urine

explanation: First morning urine is the most concentrated, meaning any early pregnancy hormones will be nice and strong and easy for the test to pick up!

question: What is the primary function of the large intestine during digestion?

options.A: Absorbing water and electrolytes
options.B: Breaking down complex proteins
options.C: Absorbing most dietary nutrients
options.D: Producing digestive enzymes

explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and leftover electrolytes from food waste to form solid feces before elimination. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the main difference between an 'illness' and a 'disease'?

options.A: Disease can be cured by nursing care, but illness requires surgery.
