options.B: Illness is a subjective feeling of being unwell, while disease is a physical alteration in body function.
options.C: Illness is diagnosed by laboratory tests, while disease is felt by the patient.
options.D: Illness only affects mental stability, whereas disease strictly affects organs.

explanation: Think of it this way: disease is the actual physical problem happening inside the body, while illness is how the patient actually experiences and feels that problem.

question: What do we call the continuous, systematic collection of health data for public health action?

options.A: Medical audit
options.B: Randomized sampling
options.C: Clinical trial
options.D: Disease surveillance

explanation: Spot on! Surveillance means keeping a steady watch on disease trends so health workers can act fast. Keep up the momentum!

question: What is the main physical outcome of body scarification?

options.A: Rapidly fading surface cuts
options.B: Deep muscle tissue damage
options.C: Permanent scars on the skin
options.D: Temporary skin discoloration

explanation: Scarification is designed to leave lasting, textured marks on the skin that stay with a person for life. Great job keeping this fundamental concept in mind!

question: Which dressing type is made from seaweed and is best suited for wounds with heavy drainage?

options.A: Dry gauze sponge
options.B: Transparent film
options.C: Alginate
options.D: Hydrocolloid

explanation: Alginate dressings absorb large amounts of wound exudate by forming a soft gel, making them ideal for bleeding or heavily draining wounds. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h4)

question: What is the main job of the circulating nurse during an operation?

options.A: Closing the surgical wound layers with sutures and staples
options.B: Managing the unsterile environment and monitoring patient safety
options.C: Performing the surgical incisions alongside the primary surgeon
options.D: Administering the general anesthetic gases to the patient

explanation: While the scrub nurse is sterile at the table, the circulating nurse moves freely around the room to coordinate supplies, record notes, and watch out for the patient's safety.

question: What is the target INR range for a standard patient taking warfarin for deep vein thrombosis?
explanation: An INR of 2.0 to 3.0 is the sweet spot for warfarin therapy—it keeps clots away without letting bleeding get out of hand. You're mastering this!

question: What do we call a disease that is always present at a steady, expected level in a specific community?

options.A: A pandemic disease
options.B: An epidemic disease
options.C: An endemic disease
options.D: A sporadic disease

explanation: You've got this! An endemic disease hangs around at a predictable, steady level in a specific area—like malaria in many parts of Nigeria—without causing sudden panic.

question: Which two medications belong to the Class IV calcium channel blocker group?

options.A: Lidocaine and flecainide
options.B: Digoxin and adenosine
options.C: Verapamil and diltiazem
options.D: Metoprolol and atenolol

explanation: Verapamil and diltiazem are non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers used to control heart rates in SVTs. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h6)

question: When would you use an independent samples t-test?

options.A: When comparing two completely separate groups of people
options.B: When there is no control group in the study
options.C: When analyzing categorical data with three or more groups
options.D: When measuring the same patients twice over time

explanation: Think 'independent = separate.' Use this when you are comparing two totally different sets of patients, like Ward A versus Ward B.

question: What is Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR)?

options.A: Energy required for vital organ function at complete rest
options.B: Calories burned only during heavy weightlifting
options.C: Total daily calories burned including all movement
options.D: The energy used solely to digest food particles

explanation: BMR is the baseline energy your body needs just to keep your heart pumping and lungs breathing while you rest quietly. No movement required!

question: How does medication non-compliance affect the wider healthcare system?

options.A: It eliminates waste by saving unused medication supplies
options.B: It increases hospital admissions and strains public health resources
options.C: It lowers the overall cost of running emergency wards
options.D: It reduces the need for expensive pharmaceutical stockpiles

explanation: Spot on. When patients skip doses, preventable complications land them right back in our hospital beds, stretching our resources thin.

question: Which cranial nerve has its main motor and sensory headquarters inside the pons?

options.A: Trigeminal nerve
options.B: Optic nerve
options.C: Hypoglossal nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

question: Why must a nurse pay attention to workplace hazards even if they currently feel strong and healthy?

options.A: Because infectious diseases disappear once they are identified
options.B: Because patients expect nurses to know about building safety
options.C: Because early awareness prevents future injury and chronic illness
options.D: Because hospital laws require passing a test every month

explanation: Many workplace risks cause slow, quiet damage over years of practice. Knowing the dangers now keeps you protected down the road.

question: What is a major equipment check the nurse must do before surgery starts?

options.A: Repairing broken video monitors during the surgical procedure
options.B: Manufacturing replacement trocars in the operating theater
options.C: Calibrating the hospital's central oxygen supply system
options.D: Ensuring all laparoscopic devices and light sources function properly

explanation: You got it! Checking cameras and lights beforehand prevents annoying and dangerous equipment failures right in the middle of the procedure.

question: Why are Infant Welfare Clinics usually set up right inside primary health care centres?

options.A: To provide specialized pediatric surgery units
options.B: To isolate sick children from the general population
options.C: To bring preventive services closer to local communities
options.D: To reduce the workload of tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Placing clinics in local primary health care centres brings essential services right to the grassroots, making it super easy for families to attend routine check-ups.

question: Why are newer drugs like solifenacin given just once a day?

options.A: They eliminate all risks of dry mouth and blurry vision
options.B: They dissolve instantly in the stomach lining
options.C: They completely bypass the liver metabolism process
options.D: They have a longer half-life to maintain steady control

explanation: Drugs with a longer half-life stay in the system longer, giving steady relief all day and making it easier for patients to remember their meds.

question: A COVID-19 patient says they feel completely fine, but their pulse oximeter reads 88% on room air. What should you do first?

options.A: Wait for the patient to request oxygen before taking any action
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink more fluids and rest in bed
options.C: Discharge the patient home since they report feeling comfortable
options.D: Apply supplemental oxygen and notify the attending healthcare provider

explanation: Spot on! An 88% saturation is a red flag regardless of how good the patient feels. Always trust your machine and act fast to protect your patient.

question: What happens to the pupils of your eyes when the parasympathetic system is stimulated?

options.A: No change in pupil size
options.B: Uncontrolled twitching
options.C: Pupil dilation
options.D: Pupil constriction

explanation: Parasympathetic signals make the circular muscles in your iris contract, which causes your pupils to constrict (get smaller). Keep going, you've got this!

question: Why do junior nurses sometimes hesitate to question unsafe orders from senior colleagues?

options.A: Hospital policies explicitly forbid questioning doctors
options.B: They possess advanced knowledge of pharmacology
options.C: Hierarchical gaps create fear of intimidation
options.D: Senior staff always make correct clinical decisions

explanation: It's a tough reality in some wards, but traditional hospital ranks can make junior staff feel too intimidated to speak up—even when a patient is at risk!

question: Why would you choose a subcutaneous injection instead of an IV for certain drugs like insulin?

options.A: To make the drug work instantly throughout the body
options.B: To bypass the need for a sterile syringe
options.C: To prevent any local skin irritation
options.D: To achieve a slow, sustained absorption rate

explanation: Spot on! Fatty tissue has fewer blood vessels than veins or muscles, which helps drugs like insulin release slowly and steadily into the body.

question: What is the primary purpose of giving antiretroviral prophylaxis to a newborn exposed to HIV?

options.A: To prevent infection from any virus acquired during delivery
options.B: To stimulate rapid weight gain in low-birth-weight infants
options.C: To cure any congenital birth defects present at birth
options.D: To boost the infant's natural vitamin absorption levels

explanation: Infant prophylaxis acts as a protective shield, clearing any viral particles that may have entered the baby's system during childbirth. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h6)

question: What is the primary driving force behind glomerular filtration?

options.A: Active muscular contraction
options.B: Ciliary movement in the tubule
options.C: Capillary blood pressure
options.D: Osmotic pull by the ureters

explanation: Hydrostatic pressure inside the glomerulus pushes fluid and small molecules across the filtration membrane without requiring cellular energy. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is it so important to have a clinic follow-up visit within 48 to 72 hours after leaving the hospital?

options.A: To check weight gain, hydration, and watch for yellow jaundice
options.B: To do the official hearing test
options.C: To give routine childhood vaccines

explanation: Those first few days at home can be tricky with feeding. An early check helps us catch weight loss, dehydration, or worsening jaundice early on!

question: What role do abnormal proteins play in degenerative neurological disorders?

options.A: They protect neurons from oxidative stress
options.B: They form harmful clumps that disrupt cell function
options.C: They speed up normal electrical signals
options.D: They help repair damaged nerve pathways

explanation: Proteins that fold incorrectly build up inside or around nerve cells, interfering with normal operations and causing cell death. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h2)

question: Which organ system is the hero for excreting non-volatile (fixed) metabolic acids from the body?

options.A: The lungs
options.B: The kidneys
options.C: The liver
options.D: The stomach

explanation: While the lungs handle volatile acids like $CO_2$, the kidneys take care of the heavy lifting by filtering out fixed metabolic acids in the urine.

question: What special addition is often necessary when a patient is placed on a very strict low protein diet?

options.A: High-sodium tablets to maintain blood pressure
options.B: Essential amino acid or keto acid supplements
options.C: Concentrated liquid sugar for quick energy
options.D: Extra doses of water-soluble vitamins only

explanation: Strict restriction removes too many vital building blocks, so medical supplements are added to prevent the body from breaking down its own muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h3)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to explain each step before starting a reproductive assessment?

options.A: To distract the patient from physical pain

options.C: To speed up the total time spent in the room
options.D: To fulfill strict legal billing requirements

explanation: Spot on! Reproductive exams can feel intimidating. Explaining what you are about to do calms nerves and helps the patient trust you.

question: A nurse gives an injection to stop heavy bleeding right after delivery. Which BEmOC signal function is this?

options.A: Execution of assisted vaginal delivery
options.B: Provision of parenteral anticonvulsants
options.C: Administration of parenteral oxytocics
options.D: Manual removal of retained placenta

explanation: Spot on! Uterotonics like oxytocin are injectable drugs used to contract the uterus and stop postpartum bleeding. A key BEmOC skill!

question: What is the main difference between physical dependence on a drug and psychological addiction?

options.A: Addiction stops the moment you lower the dose
options.B: Dependence only happens to people who abuse drugs
options.C: Dependence is a normal body adaptation, while addiction involves strong cravings
options.D: Dependence stops future pain relief from working

explanation: Physical dependence just means your body gets used to a medicine and reacts if you stop too fast. Addiction is a brain disease marked by compulsive cravings and loss of control.

question: What is the main goal of performing CPR on a patient in cardiac arrest?

options.A: To cool down the body and protect the brain
options.B: To clear thick mucus from blocked airways
options.C: To restore normal heart rhythm immediately
options.D: To keep oxygenated blood flowing to vital organs

explanation: CPR acts as an artificial pump to circulate remaining oxygen in the blood to the brain and heart until advanced help arrives. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is the Trait theory considered a bit limited in modern nursing?

options.A: It requires every nurse to have advanced surgical training
options.B: It focuses too much on patient vital signs instead of administration
options.C: It ignores how leadership skills can be learned and shaped by situations
options.D: It proves that nurses never make good ward managers

explanation: While personal traits matter, Trait theory forgets that anyone can learn leadership skills and adapt to different situations on the ward.

question: How does the medicine lactulose help a patient with liver confusion (hepatic encephalopathy)?

options.A: By increasing blood pressure in the portal vein
options.B: By stimulating the liver to produce more albumin
options.C: By trapping ammonia in the gut and helping pass it out
options.D: By killing viruses attacking the liver cells

explanation: Lactulose makes the bowel acidic, trapping ammonia so the body can flush it out in the stool instead of letting it reach the brain.

question: What is the name of the vulnerable zone where columnar and squamous epithelium meet on the cervix?

options.A: Peritoneal cavity
options.B: Transformation zone
options.C: Vaginal fornix
options.D: Endometrial cavity

question: What does Gross National Product (GNP) measure?

options.A: The total amount of physical cash printed by the central bank
options.B: Only the money earned by foreign companies inside the country
options.C: The total cost of running public hospitals for one year
options.D: The total economic value produced by a country's citizens globally

explanation: Think of GNP as tracking the wealth created by a country's people, no matter where in the world they are working! You've got this.

question: Why do water-soluble vitamins dissolve easily in our blood?

options.A: They are built from long chains of saturated fatty acids
options.B: They consist entirely of interlocking cholesterol rings
options.C: Their chemical structures contain many polar groups
options.D: They contain heavy mineral salt deposits

explanation: Like dissolves like! Polar parts of the vitamin love interacting with water, allowing them to travel smoothly through the bloodstream.

question: What does the letter 'A' stand for in the SBAR communication framework?

options.A: Assessment
options.B: Antibiotic
options.C: Admission
options.D: Aftercare

question: Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB) means the bacteria are resistant to which two key drugs?

options.B: Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide

question: Why should you always look closely at the tip of the nasogastric tube right after removing it?

options.A: To measure the patient's stomach length

options.C: To make sure the whole tube came out in one piece and nothing broke off inside

explanation: Checking the removed tube ensures no broken bits were left behind in the patient's stomach or food pipe. A quick glance saves a lot of trouble!

question: A patient takes daily medication that successfully controls their high blood pressure. However, they feel drained, skip workouts, and eat junk food. Where do they fit on the wellness scale?

options.A: Completely outside the continuum because they take medication
options.B: At the far left end experiencing premature death
options.C: In the neutral point, free of disease symptoms but below optimal wellness
options.D: At the far right end representing high-level wellness

explanation: Spot on! Keeping symptoms under control puts them in the safe middle zone. True wellness takes a bit more active care with lifestyle habits.

question: Which layer of the gut wall is directly responsible for pushing food forward with wave-like squeezes?

options.A: Muscularis externa
options.B: Mucosa

options.D: Serosa

question: Why is having clear rules for DRF exemptions so important for hospital staff?

options.A: It stops staff from showing personal bias when giving out free drugs
options.B: It allows the pharmacy to increase drug prices for wealthy patients
options.C: It ensures that doctors do not have to write any medical prescriptions
options.D: It guarantees that the federal government will pay the hospital bonus funds

explanation: Clear criteria remove guesswork and favoritism, making sure that only genuinely qualified patients receive free medications.

question: What is the main goal of giving recommendations for future research?

options.A: To give graduate students easy thesis topics they do not have to think about
options.B: To guide subsequent studies based on current gaps and unanswered questions
options.C: To prove that the current study answered every single question in nursing
options.D: To ensure the original researcher gets paid for all future grants

explanation: You've got this! No single study answers everything. Pointing out what's left to discover helps the next wave of researchers.

question: How do nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockers stop a muscle from contracting?

options.C: By destroying acetylcholine before it reaches the nerve ending

question: What common barrier often affects contraceptive uptake in resource-constrained Nigerian communities?

options.B: Financial constraints and out-of-pocket supply costs

options.D: Laws that ban nurses from discussing birth control openly

question: What type of medicine is often given to hospitalized COVID-19 patients to prevent blood clots?

options.C: Antihistamines
options.D: Antibiotics

question: Why must nurses care about how medications are stored on the ward?

options.A: Pharmaceutical companies only trust nurses with liquid medications

options.C: Nurses handle drugs from the supply point to actual bedside administration

question: Which of the following is NOT a reliable way to measure the true success of a BCC program?

question: A patient is recovering from a myomectomy. Which sign means you should call the doctor immediately?

explanation: Sharp, severe pain and heavy bleeding after pelvic surgery are major warning signs of internal bleeding or complications that need fast medical action.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard criterion for selecting an essential drug?

options.A: Bright packaging color and appealing flavor
options.B: High public health relevance
options.C: Proven clinical efficacy and safety
options.D: Acceptable cost-effectiveness

explanation: Aesthetic features like color and flavor do not determine whether a drug is medically essential for public health. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of restorative nursing care in an SNF?

options.A: To reinforce therapy goals during everyday routine activities
options.B: To administer complex intravenous medications overnight
options.C: To replace formal physical therapy sessions entirely
options.D: To manage facility financial records and insurance claims

explanation: Restorative nursing helps residents practice their therapy skills during daily routines so they can hold onto their independence.

question: Why is you, the bedside nurse, so important in hospital waste management?

options.A: Nurses write all national environmental health laws
options.B: Nurses are solely responsible for incinerator operations
options.C: Nurses supervise the daily clinical actions at the point of generation
options.D: Nurses purchase all hospital disposal bins

explanation: Spot on! Because you provide direct patient care every day, you control how waste is sorted and handled right at the bedside.

question: Where does the lengthwise growth of a long bone happen?

options.A: Periosteal collar
options.B: Medullary cavity
options.C: Epiphyseal plate
options.D: Articular capsule

explanation: You'll hear this called the growth plate! The epiphyseal plate is packed with active cartilage cells that keep pushing bones to grow longer during childhood.

question: In stroke care, what does 'spasticity' mean?

options.A: Rapid wasting away of muscle tissue
options.B: Complete loss of all muscle sensation
options.C: Uncontrolled trembling during resting states
options.D: Involuntary muscle stiffness and tight spasms

explanation: Spot on! Spasticity is when muscles become tight and stiff because of nerve damage, making them hard to stretch out.

question: A patient asks why her injectable birth control takes months to wear off after her scheduled date. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: The medicine travels directly to the brain and stays in the neurons
options.B: The injection forms a slow-release depot store in the muscle tissue
options.C: The drug permanently alters the DNA structure of the ovaries
options.D: The liver stores the chemical in fat cells for future energy use

explanation: Injectables like DMPA are designed as a "depot" injection, meaning the muscle holds onto the medicine and releases it slowly into the body over a few months.

question: What should a nurse tell a patient taking liquid iron syrup to prevent staining their teeth?

options.A: Drink the liquid through a straw and rinse your mouth afterwards.
options.B: Take the medication right before lying down to go to sleep at night.
options.C: Brush your teeth vigorously immediately after swallowing the dose.
options.D: Mix the iron directly into a full glass of whole milk before drinking.

explanation: Liquid iron can easily stain teeth! Using a straw bypasses the teeth, and rinsing washes away any lingering drops. Simple practical nursing advice!

question: A patient has both hookworms and roundworms at the same time. What kind of drug property do you need?

options.A: Strict specificity for a single parasite enzyme
options.B: Ability to cross the blood-brain barrier easily
options.C: Broad-spectrum activity against multiple nematode species
options.D: Rapid elimination through the renal system

explanation: You got it! Broad-spectrum drugs are fantastic because they tackle several different worm species in one go.

question: A patient taking oral metronidazole complains of stomach upset. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Crush the tablets and mix them into a citrus fruit juice
options.B: Double the next dose to compensate for the upset stomach
options.C: Take the medication with food or milk to ease gastric irritation
options.D: Stop taking the medication immediately and discard the remaining pills

explanation: Correct! Metronidazole can be tough on the tummy, but taking it with meals or milk helps soothe the stomach without losing drug power.

question: What special X-ray technology does the radiologist use to watch the barium move in real-time?

options.A: Thermography
options.B: Electrocardiography
options.C: Fluoroscopy
options.D: Magnetic resonance

explanation: Keep it up! Fluoroscopy is basically an X-ray movie, letting the doctor watch the drink flow through your system live. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h5)

question: Why is a rise in pressure inside the skull so harmful to the brain?

options.A: It immediately destroys the myelin sheath surrounding peripheral nerves
options.B: It triggers an excessive production of cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles
options.C: It causes the skull bones to expand and fracture outward
options.D: It squeezes blood vessels and reduces the flow of oxygen to brain cells

explanation: Makes total sense, right? The skull can't stretch, so high pressure squeezes the tiny blood vessels shut, cutting off vital oxygen to brain cells.

question: What kind of trouble does a nurse face for leaving their duty post without official permission?

options.A: An automatic promotion to a higher administrative grade level
options.B: A commendation letter from the hospital management board
options.C: Immediate conversion of the absence into paid study leave
options.D: Severe administrative penalties for gross misconduct

explanation: Absconding or leaving work without approval is treated as truancy and attracts serious disciplinary action. Always secure your leave first!

question: Why don't doctors do throat swabs for every person who walks in with a mild cold?

options.A: Most common colds are viral and resolve with supportive care
options.B: Laboratory tests are completely inaccurate for respiratory illnesses
options.C: Testing always causes severe physical trauma to the throat
options.D: Viral infections require immediate intravenous antibiotics

explanation: Exactly! Since normal colds are viral and clear up on their own, testing and antibiotics aren't needed—just rest and fluids.

question: When should a nurse manager consider revising an existing objective?

options.A: Only when ordered by hospital accountants at the end of the year.
options.B: As soon as the first week of the planning cycle has passed.
options.C: Whenever staff members complain that the work is slightly difficult.
options.D: When unexpected events like a staff shortage or outbreak change clinical conditions.

explanation: Life in a clinic can be unpredictable. When things like sudden outbreaks or staff shortages happen, our plans need to be flexible enough to adapt.

question: How is the autonomic nervous system different from the somatic nervous system?

options.A: The autonomic system is completely independent and never interacts with the brain.
options.B: The autonomic system controls involuntary organs while the somatic controls voluntary muscles.
options.C: The autonomic system only uses sensory neurons while the somatic uses motor neurons.
options.D: The autonomic system is located in the brain while the somatic is in the spinal cord.

explanation: Spot on! Somatic nerves let you move your arms and legs on purpose, while autonomic pathways handle the behind-the-scenes organs that work without your direct control.

question: What should you do if the chosen injection site has an open sore or infection?

options.A: Warm the skin with a hot pack to improve blood flow
options.B: Choose a different healthy site for the injection
options.C: Use a longer needle to bypass the damaged area
options.D: Clean the sore with extra antiseptic before piercing

explanation: Always protect broken skin! Finding a healthy site prevents spreading infection and helps the medication absorb properly.

question: Your patient has a poor appetite and struggles to finish large meal trays, but they really need extra protein. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Scold the patient for not finishing their assigned food tray
options.B: Remove all food trays until the patient asks for a big meal
options.C: Switch the patient immediately to a clear liquid diet
options.D: Provide smaller, frequent high-protein snacks throughout the day

explanation: Large plates can overwhelm a weak patient. Giving smaller, nutrient-packed snacks across the day makes eating much less stressful and very achievable.

question: What is the primary benefit of choosing the rectal route in clinical practice?

options.A: It guarantees faster absorption than an intravenous injection
options.B: It provides a dependable alternative when oral intake is blocked
options.C: It is the most comfortable method for long-term daily drug use
options.D: It completely eliminates all side effects of strong medications

explanation: Patients who are unconscious or vomiting heavily still need critical medications, making the rectum a practical backup route. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h1)

question: As a nurse, what is the quickest way to help a patient who is suddenly struggling to catch their breath due to lung cancer?

options.A: Laying the patient flat on their back in bed
options.B: Placing the patient in a high-Fowler's position
options.C: Encouraging rapid, shallow mouth breathing
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake for twelve hours

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Sitting the patient upright in a high-Fowler's position lets their chest expand fully, making it much easier to draw breath.

question: Why do midwives use absorbable threads (sutures) for repairing perineal tears?

options.A: The body breaks them down naturally, so the mother doesn't need a visit just to remove stitches
options.B: They are the only threads that never cause allergies
options.C: They change color to warn you if an infection starts
options.D: They dissolve the second they touch warm water

explanation: Absorbable sutures save new mums the stress and discomfort of coming back to the clinic just to get stitches pulled out!

question: Why is keeping track of a home care patient's weight so important over time?

options.A: It provides an objective trend of whether the patient's nutritional plan is working.
options.B: It predicts the exact date of patient recovery.
options.C: It is required to calculate the patient's daily medication doses.
options.D: It measures the exact amount of water stored in the lungs.

explanation: We might not notice slow changes just by looking at someone. Regular weigh-ins give us clear proof of whether our nutrition plan is helping them thrive or needs tweaking.

question: How do the fallopian tubes move an egg toward the uterus?

options.A: Using tiny waving cilia and smooth muscle contractions
options.B: By producing strong chemical suction currents
options.C: Using pulsating pressure from nearby arterial blood flow
options.D: Through rapid gravity shifts in the pelvic cavity

explanation: Correct! Tiny hair-like cilia wave back and forth while the tube muscles gently push the egg along on its journey.

question: What is the main purpose of reflective practice in nursing?

options.A: To punish staff members who make clinical mistakes
options.B: To turn everyday experience into professional growth
options.C: To replace the formal nursing assessment process
options.D: To reduce the paperwork required at shift handover

explanation: Reflective practice allows nurses to learn from past situations and improve future care. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which condition is a clear contraindication for routine nasotracheal suctioning?

options.A: Severe bleeding disorders or severe nasal trauma
options.B: Needing a routine check of vital signs every four hours
options.C: A mild low-grade fever without respiratory changes
options.D: Being sleepy but easily waking up when spoken to

explanation: Passing a catheter through a damaged or bleeding nose can cause dangerous hemorrhage and further trauma. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h2)

question: How are special senses different from general senses?

options.A: Special senses are housed in complex, distinct organs in the head
options.B: Special senses only function while a person is sleeping
options.C: General senses do not use electrical impulses to communicate
options.D: General senses are controlled entirely by the spinal cord

explanation: Unlike touch receptors that are spread all over your body, special senses like sight, taste, and hearing have their own specialized, dedicated homes in the head, like the eyes and tongue!

question: What does the liver produce when the body burns a lot of fat for fuel because carbohydrate levels are very low?

options.A: Nucleic acids
options.B: Ketone bodies
options.C: Lactic acids
options.D: Plasma proteins

explanation: When carbs are scarce and the body relies heavily on fat, the liver creates ketone bodies as an alternative fuel source, especially for the brain.

question: What is the big advantage of using the 'closed gloving' technique in theater?

options.A: It prevents bare hands from touching the outside of the sterile gloves
options.B: It eliminates the need to wear a surgical gown during the case
options.C: It keeps the sterile gloves warmer during long procedures
options.D: It allows the nurse to scrub hands much faster than usual

explanation: By keeping your hands tucked inside your gown sleeves, you can slide your gloves on without your bare skin ever touching the outside surface.

question: Which of these conditions can cause sudden swelling of the soft tissues in the upper airway?

options.A: Pulmonary embolism
options.B: Anaphylaxis
options.C: Chronic bronchitis
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: Anaphylaxis is a severe allergic reaction. It can cause rapid swelling in the face, tongue, and throat, which can dangerously close off the upper airway in minutes.

question: What is the correct way to apply prophylactic eye ointment in a newborn?

options.A: Flood the entire closed eyelid with liquid solution
options.B: Massage the upper eyelid vigorously after application
options.C: Apply into the lower conjunctival sac without touching the eye
options.D: Place the ointment directly onto the center of the cornea

explanation: Spot on! Putting it in the lower sac keeps the tube clean and protects the baby's eye from accidental injury. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: A manager wants to introduce a new clinical audit system with minimal staff pushback. What is the best approach?

options.A: Install hidden security cameras in the nurses' station without telling anyone
options.B: Threatened immediate termination for anyone who questions the audit schedule
options.C: Involve frontline nurses in designing the standards and explain the safety benefits
options.D: Keep all performance data completely secret from the nursing staff

explanation: When you involve staff in the process, they build trust, feel valued, and truly understand why the safety controls matter.

question: What is a major risk if a hydatid cyst spills its contents inside the body?

options.A: Dissemination and formation of multiple secondary cysts
options.B: Immediate complete cure of the parasitic infection
options.C: Rapid calcification and harmless absorption
options.D: Permanent immunity against future tapeworm contact

explanation: If live cells spill out, they can plant themselves in new spots and grow into a bunch of brand-new secondary cysts.

question: Why do traditional health clinics often make teenage patients feel unwelcome?

options.A: They only open during late night hours when teenagers are in school
options.B: They are required by law to report all visits to local police stations
options.C: They completely lack basic medical equipment for younger populations
options.D: They are usually structured and designed primarily for adults or young children

explanation: Standard clinics often overlook the specific developmental, social, and emotional needs of teenagers, making them feel out of place. You've got this!

question: Why is a patient simply nodding and smiling an unreliable sign that they understand?

options.A: Nodding only indicates physical tiredness
options.B: Patients cannot hear the nurse while nodding
options.C: Patients often nod out of politeness or fear rather than comprehension
options.D: It means the patient disagrees with the plan

explanation: Exactly. Many people will just nod politely to a nurse or doctor even when they are totally confused. Always double-check!

question: What happens to a patient's lung if air or fluid gets inside the pleural space?

options.A: The lung remains completely unaffected by the trapped air
options.B: The lung expands rapidly due to increased volume
options.C: The lung fills entirely with blood instead of air
options.D: The lung collapses because negative pressure is lost

explanation: Spot on! When air or fluid enters where it shouldn't, it breaks that delicate vacuum, causing the lung to pull away and collapse.

question: How soon can a woman theoretically start ovulating again after experiencing an abortion?

options.A: Never until she reaches menopause
options.B: Only after six full months have passed
options.C: Exactly one full year following treatment
options.D: As early as two weeks post-procedure

explanation: Fertility can bounce back remarkably fast after pregnancy termination, which is why birth control counseling must happen immediately during the PAC visit.

question: How does hyperparathyroidism usually impact a patient's bones?

options.A: It forces extra calcium to deposit, making bones overly thick
options.B: It triggers rapid bone growth that crushes nearby nerve roots
options.C: It stops blood flow to the joints, causing cartilage to melt
options.D: It pulls calcium out of bones, making them weak and painful

explanation: Too much parathyroid hormone acts like a withdrawal slip, pulling calcium right out of the skeleton and leaving bones fragile and aching.

question: A resident needs physical help to cut their food and bring it to their mouth. Which daily living activity does this fall under?

options.A: Bathing
options.B: Feeding
options.C: Transferring
options.D: Toileting

explanation: Well done! Eating and drinking assistance is classified under the feeding category of ADLs.

question: What is a great benefit of using the vaginal route for misoprostol?

options.A: It works instantly in under five minutes
options.B: It means you don't need to know how far along the pregnancy is
options.C: It completely stops all cramping pain
options.D: It results in fewer gastrointestinal side effects like nausea

explanation: Vaginal use skips the stomach processing, which helps many patients avoid nasty stomach upset and vomiting. Smart clinical choice!

question: How does proper birth spacing directly help keep mothers safe?

options.A: By reducing complications like severe bleeding and exhausted uterine muscles
options.B: By ensuring all deliveries happen exclusively at home
options.C: By guaranteeing that mothers will never experience morning sickness
options.D: By completely eliminating the need for antenatal care visits

explanation: You've got this! Proper spacing gives the uterus time to rest between pregnancies, which greatly lowers the risk of heavy bleeding (hemorrhage). Great nursing insight to keep in mind!

question: Besides eating healthy food, what is the big benefit of practicing portion control?

options.A: Maintaining energy balance and preventing excessive weight gain
options.B: Ensuring that digestion takes place only during nighttime hours
options.C: Eliminating the need to consume any carbohydrates at all
options.D: Reducing the body's overall requirement for clean drinking water

explanation: Exactly. Portion control stops us from taking in more energy than we burn off, helping us stay at a healthy weight.

question: Why is the CSSD so important for infection control?

options.A: It breaks the chain of infection by providing sterile instruments
options.B: It administers routine vaccinations to hospital staff
options.C: It isolates patients with contagious airborne diseases
options.D: It monitors patient antibiotic resistance patterns daily

explanation: By making sure every tool is thoroughly decontaminated and germ-free, CSSD stops infections from spreading from one patient to another.
